stem.en: A stone of mass 2 kg is dropped from rest from a height of 5 m onto soft sand, and stops in the sand. Take g = 10 m/s^2. How much work does the sand do on the stone while stopping it? Give the size of the work, without a sign, in joules.

explanation.en: At the top the stone has U = mgh = 2 x 10 x 5 = 100 J. Just before it hits the sand, all of this is kinetic energy. The sand must take away all 100 J to stop it, so the sand does 100 J of work on the stone (negative in sign, because it pushes against the motion).

hints.en: Find the stone's potential energy at the start.
The sand removes all the energy the stone has when it lands.
